title: Electric Flux and Gauss's Law

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 12 — Electric Charges and Fields

explanation: Gauss's law relates the total electric flux through any closed surface to the net charge enclosed within it, independent of the surface's shape/size and independent of charges outside it. It is most useful as a calculation shortcut for highly symmetric charge distributions, where a Gaussian surface can be chosen so E is uniform and known everywhere on it.

variables.meaning: Electric flux through the closed surface
Net charge enclosed by the surface

workedExample.scenario: A charge of +5 μC is enclosed by an arbitrary closed surface.

commonMistakes: Assuming flux depends on the surface's exact shape or size — for a fixed enclosed charge, flux through ANY closed surface is identical.
Including charges OUTSIDE the Gaussian surface in qenclosed — only charge strictly inside the closed surface counts, even though outside charges can still affect the field's local value/direction.
genZNote: Gauss's law doesn't care about the shape of your surface — only what charge is trapped inside counts.
